title: Tower of Nodes (unique_ptr)

links.title: C++ Core Guidelines R.20: use unique_ptr or shared_ptr to represent ownership

hints: push: the new node takes ownership of the old head: head_ = std::make_unique<Node>(Node{value, std::move(head_)});
pop: save the value, then head_ = std::move(head_->next); - the old top node is destroyed automatically.
A unique_ptr cannot be copied, only moved: every transfer of ownership is a visible std::move.

The million-node test: the default destructor destroys node 1, whose member destroys node 2, whose member... one nested call per node, until the call stack overflows. Write ~Stack() as a loop: while (head_) head_ = std::move(head_->next);
